results.question: When is the professional admission process automatically performed for qualifying computer science students?
results.gold_answer: At the end of the sophomore year.
results.answer: After being admitted to the college, students desiring to pursue a degree in computer science must go through the Professional Admission process, which is automatically performed for qualifying students at the end of the sophomore year. results.question: What percentage of attempted credit hours must undergraduates complete to meet SAP pace requirements?
results.gold_answer: 67 percent.
results.answer: This SAP policy requirement is known as the Minimum Pace Requirement (Pace) and is calculated as follows: Completed (earned) UNL credit hours [with grades of A through D or P (Pass)] divided by all attempted UNL credit hours (this includes: earned credit hours plus incomplete, failed, no pass, withdrawn credit hours). This SAP policy requirement is known as the Minimum Pace Requirement (Pace) and is calculated as follows: Completed (earned) UNL credit hours [with grades of A through D or P (Pass)] divided by all attempted UNL credit hours (this includes: earned credit hours plus incomplete, failed, no pass or withdrawn credit hours). [S1] [S2]

results.question: What cumulative GPA must undergraduates maintain after four or more semesters to meet SAP?
results.gold_answer: A 2.000 cumulative GPA.
results.answer:
A student can either successfully appeal for reinstatement of their financial aid eligibility (See Appeal Process below) or they can earn both the necessary cumulative GPA and meet the minimum completion rate of the SAP for Financial Aid Recipients Policy while paying for their enrollment on their own. In order to meet SAP standards, students must:
Complete at least 67% of all attempted credit hours (with satisfactory grades),
Earn a minimum 2.000 GPA by the fourth semester of enrollment at UNL (undergraduate students),
Complete a degree within the maximum timeframe allowed, and
Not be academically dismissed from the University (readmitted students must still meet all SAP requirements should they wish to receive financial aid). [S1] [S2]

results.question: How does academic bankruptcy affect SAP calculations?
results.gold_answer: It may improve SAP GPA, but the bankrupted attempted and earned hours still remain in SAP calculations.
results.answer:
Academic Bankruptcy:
While Academic Bankruptcy will improve your SAP cumulative GPA as it does with your academic record, the UNL credit hours attempted and earned that have been "bankrupted" will remain part of the SAP calculation. Academic Bankruptcy does not forgive attempted credit hours in the SAP calculation. [S1] [S2]
